Contributing to nflfastR

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Thanks for your interest in contributing! Issues and pull requests are welcome, from people and from AI agents.

If the play-by-play data of nflfastR is wrong, there are two possible reasons:

  1. The parser has a bug or doesn’t handle a situation correctly. Please open an issue that shows the problem (game ID, play ID, column, expected and actual value) or a pull request that fixes the parser.
  2. The raw data is wrong. If the error follows a rule that can apply to other games too, it is fixed in the parser as well. If the raw data has a few wrong values in a few games and no rule finds them, they are fixed with a patch, see below.

Patching errors of the raw data

inst/pbp_patches.dcf lists single errors of the raw data. nflfastR applies these patches while it parses a game, before it computes anything from the data, so a patch also changes everything derived from the patched value (e.g. EPA and win probability).

Patch or parser fix?

  • Fix the parser if the error follows a rule that can apply to other games too (e.g. all Jacksonville home games of 2001 and 2002 name the same team on every play), or if the fix has to compute values (e.g. the first downs of a game in which the NFL didn’t record them).
  • Add a patch if the raw data has a few wrong values in a few games and no rule finds them.

Format

The file has the format of an R DESCRIPTION file (DCF): one record per patch, records separated by an empty line, one field: value per line. A long value can continue on the next lines if they are indented. Leave out the fields a patch doesn’t use; a field that is left out is NA. Keep the records sorted by game_id, play_id, action, stat_id and column (the tests check this).

field meaning
game_id nflfastR game ID
play_id play ID. Left out in a set patch: all plays of the game
action drop_play, drop_stat or set, see below
stat_id the stat ID of a drop_stat patch
column the column of a set patch
from the value of column the raw data has now, left out for NA
to the correct value, left out for NA
reason what is wrong, with the issue number if there is one

For example:

game_id: 2011_13_DET_NO
play_id: 1152
action: drop_play
reason: duplicated touchdown record (one for each team) that counts the
  points twice

game_id: 2012_04_NO_GB
play_id: 1085
action: set
column: time
from: 03:33
to: 03:34
reason: wrong game clock

  • drop_play removes the play from the raw plays, before anything is derived from it. Use it for plays the raw data has twice.

  • drop_stat removes all rows of the stat ID on the play from the raw play stats, before the stat columns (rush_attempt, passer_player_id, td_team, …) are derived from them. Prefer it to set patches of stat columns, because one stat ID sets several columns that must agree.

  • set changes the value of column after the plays are parsed, before anything is derived from it (e.g. yardline_100 from yrdln). The columns that the parser computes again later (posteam, goal_to_go and the team columns td_team, penalty_team, safety_team, return_team, fumble_recovery_1_team and timeout_team) are patched after that. Some columns of the final data don’t exist at this point, because they have another name or are derived from another column. Patch the column in the right column of this table instead (the error of a patch of such a column names it too):

    final data patch file
    desc play_description
    qtr quarter
    quarter_end play_description (the text “END QUARTER”)
    side_of_field, yardline_100 yardline
    ydstogo yards_to_go
    yrdln yardline

    Columns that are derived from several others (e.g. ep) or from the play stats (use drop_stat patches) can’t be patched.

    play_type is derived later from play_type_nfl and the play description (e.g. kneel downs and spikes). A patch of play_type_nfl changes play_type_nfl, but not necessarily play_type.

    from and to are converted to the class of the column. The value is only changed if it is from on all patched plays.

drop_play and drop_stat patches also apply to the play stats that calculate_stats() uses. These are built separately (release playstats of nflverse/nflverse-pbp), so a new patch reaches calculate_stats() once they are rebuilt. set patches only change the play-by-play data.

A patch that doesn’t fit the raw data (a missing play or stat, a value other than from) warns with class nflfastR_patch_not_applied and changes nothing. build_nflfastR_pbp() and fast_scraper() muffle these warnings, because they are for the maintainers: the weekly check below reports them. A set patch of a column that doesn’t exist or with a value that can’t be converted is an error, and build_nflfastR_pbp() skips the game, so the tests check both for the patches in the file.

Checking and cleaning the patches

The raw data and the parser change, so a patch can become unnecessary. check_pbp_patches() (internal) checks every patch against the current raw data and parser and lists the patches that

  • are obsolete: the raw data was fixed, i.e. the column of a set patch has the value to now,
  • are unused: they are applied, but the play-by-play data (and for drop_stat the play stats) is the same without them, e.g. because the parser handles the error now,
  • don’t fit for another reason (a missing play or stat, a value other than from and to). A missing play or stat isn’t obsolete for sure, because the NFL may have changed its ID and kept the error.
devtools::load_all()
check_pbp_patches()
# removes the obsolete and unused patches from inst/pbp_patches.dcf
check_pbp_patches(prune = TRUE)

Pruning leaves the other records as they are. Patches that don’t fit for another reason need a look, because the error may still be there with other play IDs or values. An online test finds patches that aren’t applied on every pull request, and the workflow check-patches.yaml runs check_pbp_patches() every week, because the raw data can change without a change of nflfastR.

Adding patches

  1. Fork the repository and create a branch.
  2. Add the records to inst/pbp_patches.dcf.
  3. devtools::test(filter = "patch") checks the format.
  4. check_pbp_patches() (after devtools::load_all()) checks that every patch fits the raw data and changes it.
  5. Build the patched games with devtools::load_all() and build_nflfastR_pbp(), and check the result.
  6. Open a pull request that names the patched games and why the raw data is wrong.

If a patched game is one of the games of the regression test, the test fails because the output changes on purpose. The maintainers update the expected output, see data-raw/test_game_selection/README.md.
